flashcards.front: Why store active moving driver coordinates in city-sharded in-memory H3/Redis rather than Postgres?
flashcards.back: 2M drivers pinging every 4s generate 500k updates/sec, which would overwhelm SQL B-Tree index writes. Yet 2M active records × 64B is only ~128 MB—fitting cleanly in sharded RAM with short TTL expiration.

quizzes.scenario: Two riders request a ride in the same millisecond near the only available driver, d_901. Both see 'Driver assigned' before one of them gets an error.
quizzes.question: What prevents the double dispatch without locking the whole city?
options: A city-level lock on the dispatch table during matching
Retry the losing rider after a random delay of 1 to 3 seconds
Faster GPS pings so both riders see the driver's state sooner
A short per-driver lock taken before the offer is sent
quizzes.explanation: Take a short per-driver lock before sending an offer, for example SET lock:driver:d_901 trip_id NX EX 15. Only one dispatch flow can offer to that driver at a time, and the TTL frees the driver if the offer is never answered.
optionExplanations: This works but blocks every other match in the city.
Retries happen after the double assignment; they do not prevent it.
Fresher location data does not stop two flows offering the same driver.
Correct. It serializes offers for one driver without a city-wide lock.
